newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle trade thin at $66 -feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle trade thin at $66 -feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle Wednesday sold steady at $66.00 per cwt in light volume, feedlot sources said.

About 1,000 head sold in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area, USDA said. About 75,000 head were confirmed sold for the week to date which included 25,900 formulated and 800 previously contracted cattle to be shipped this week.
About 3,700 head had sold in Kansas, bringing the week-to-date count to 93,300, including 14,100 contracted or formulated cattle.
Feedlot operators were bracing for another bout of extremely cold and windy weather seen moving into the Plains Thursday.
Wind chill readings on Thursday were forecast to drop to minus 55 Fahrenheit in Nebraska and minus 30 F in the Texas Panhandle.

The weather will set cattle back on weight gains in most areas, sources said. Cold will have its most dangerous impact in northeast Nebraska, where feedlots reported three to five percent death loss after nearly a month of severe winter weather, Nebraska Cattleman Association said.
